question: Both the European Railway Agency and the Commission have repeatedly stated that the Spanish Government must commission an independent investigation into the Alvia railway accident of 24 July 2013 in Santiago de Compostela with 80 fatalities.

However, throughout this period, Spain’s Railway Accidents Investigation Committee (CIAF) has continuously opposed an independent technical investigation with the backing of four different governments and five Spanish Ministers for Development, both from the PP and the PSOE.

In view of this non-compliance, the refusal to carry out an independent investigation will shortly be examined by the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg, which has agreed to consider the case brought by victims of the accident. 1.
Is the Commission aware of this situation?
Will the Commission insist that CIAF ensure that an independent investigation into the accident is carried out?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.5.2025) The Commission takes note of the information provided by the Honourable Member. Given that the applicable legal framework remains unchanged, the Commission refers the Honourable Member to its reply to the parliamentary question E-000669/2024 in which the Commission stated that the obligation to ensure that an investigation is carried out after any serious accident on the Union rail system rests fully with the Member States.
